title: What are you doing? — actions in progress
goal: Say what is happening right now with the -ছি ending, and learn a Bengali habit English doesn't have: saying goodbye with “I'm coming”, not “I'm going”.
bekal: form the progressive: করছি, যাচ্ছি, খাচ্ছি
tell আমি করি (habit) from আমি করছি (right now)
use the progressive for fixed near-future plans
handle a phone call with standard phrases
say goodbye with আসি and আসছি

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — A phone call from the market
dialogs.intro: Ani calls Mitali from the market because she has forgotten the name of the vegetable she was supposed to buy. Notice the -ছি ending in almost every line — it signals that the action is happening at that very moment.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I'm at the market. I'm buying vegetables.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Good! Mom is cooking right now.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: What is she cooking? I can't smell it from here!
lines.literal: what — cooking — is-doing? smell — here — from — am-getting — not — you-know!

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Ha ha! She's frying fish. What are you looking for?
lines.literal: ha ha! fish — is-frying. you(polite) — what — are-looking-for?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I've forgotten the name of that green vegetable.
lines.literal: that — green — vegetable-the-'s — name — forgetting — have-gone.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Bottle gourd? Or pui greens? Send a photo.
lines.literal: bottle-gourd? or — pui-greens? a-little — photo — send.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Sending it. Hold on, the seller is calling me.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Did you get it? This one, right?

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Yes, that's bottle gourd. Take two. When are you coming back?
lines.literal: yes, that — bottle-gourd. two — take. you(polite) — when — are-returning?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I'm on my way right now. Ten minutes!

notes: **The progressive is made by inserting -ছ- before the ordinary ending.** করি → কর**ছি**, করেন → কর**ছেন**, করে → কর**ছে**. The four endings you learned in unit 6 stay the same; the only new thing is one syllable in the middle. ⚠️ For verbs ending in a vowel, ছ doubles to চ্ছ: যাওয়া → **যাচ্ছি**, খাওয়া → **খাচ্ছি**, পাঠানো → **পাঠাচ্ছি**.

**The difference between করি and করছি is exactly “I work” versus “I'm working”.** আমি রোজ কাজ করি (I work every day — habit) versus আমি এখন কাজ করছি (I'm working now). English marks it with *-ing*; Bengali with an infix. Since English already draws this line, this unit should feel easy.

⚠️ **Bengali uses the progressive in some places English doesn't.** In live conversation, আমি বুঝছি না (I'm not understanding) sounds more natural than আমি বুঝি না. When in doubt in a face-to-face exchange, the progressive is almost always the safe choice.

**The progressive is also used for fixed plans.** আমি কাল যাচ্ছি means “I'm leaving tomorrow” — exactly like English *I'm leaving tomorrow*. ⚠️ What sets it apart from the true future (unit 18) is certainty: যাচ্ছি means the ticket is already bought.

⚠️ **Verbs that raise their vowel raise it for EVERY person in the progressive.** In the simple present, শোনা raises only for আমি (শুনি, but তুমি শোনো). In the progressive, all of them raise: **শুনছি, শুনছ, শুনছেন, শুনছে**. Likewise বুঝছি, লিখছি, দিচ্ছি, নিচ্ছি. This actually simplifies things — one stem for the whole row.

**Say goodbye with “I'm coming”, not “I'm going”.** The most common parting phrase isn't “I'm going” but **আসি** (*a-si* — I come) or **আসছি** (I'm coming). The reason is old but still felt: saying “I'm going” is considered bad luck, as if you'll never come back. ⚠️ If someone says আসি while waving, they're leaving, not announcing their arrival.

**Phone calls have their own phrases.** হ্যালো to answer, **কে বলছেন?** (who's speaking?), **একটু ধরুন** (hold on — literally “hold a little”), **শুনতে পাচ্ছি না** (I can't hear you), **রাখছি** (I'm hanging up — literally “I'm putting it down”). These four cover almost every beginner's phone call.

grammars.title: The progressive — ঘটমান বর্তমান
after: **The negative is still না at the end:** আমি বুঝছি না (I'm not understanding), সে আসছে না (he/she isn't coming). ⚠️ There's no special negative form; the unit 6 rule applies as is.

grammars.title: Phone phrases and everyday goodbyes

head: বাংলা
Say it
Meaning
rows: I'll hang up now — take care.

after: ⚠️ **ভালো থাকবেন is the warmest and safest goodbye** for anyone — literally “may you stay well”. In everyday conversation it's used more than আল্লাহ হাফেজ or নমস্কার, and it suits shopkeepers, neighbors, and bosses alike.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Fish is more than a side dish
items: **মাছে ভাতে বাঙালি** (*ma-chhé bha-té ban-ga-li*) — “a Bengali is fish and rice”. This saying is no joke: fish and rice are the core of daily food, and asking someone which fish they like best is an opener that never fails.
**ইলিশ** *ilish* — hilsa, the most revered fish in Bengal, with a price that can shock beginners. Mention it with due reverence and you'll instantly sound like an insider.
**At the market, fish is sold by the কেজি and often cut on the spot.** Useful phrases: **কেটে দিন** (*kè-Té din* — please cut it) and **আজকের মাছ?** (*aj-kér machh* — today's fish?).

blocks.text: One lovely habit at Bengal's markets: after weighing, the seller almost always adds **a little something for free** — a sprig of coriander, a chili, a piece of ginger. It has no official name, but the meaning is clear: you're a regular, not just a buyer. Accept it with a **ধন্যবাদ** and a smile, and your next visit will be much warmer — and often cheaper, too.

exercises.prompt: Choose the simple present or the progressive.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: আমি অপেক্ষা করছি। — শুনতে পাচ্ছি না। — আম্মা কী রান্না করছেন? — এখনই আসছি, দশ মিনিট। — আমি বাজারে সবজি কিনছি।
আপনি কী করছেন? — আমি সবজি কিনছি। — শুনতে পাচ্ছি না। — একটু ধরুন, আমি আসছি। — আম্মা মাছ ভাজছেন। — পরে ফোন করছি।
